title: Core: workflow engine — match triggers, schedule actions
description: src/youtrack_aitrack/engine/. WorkflowEngine.dispatch(event, workflows) finds workflows whose trigger matches, then executes their action graph respecting depends_on. Independent actions run in asyncio.gather. Run lifecycle: pending->running->done|failed. Per-action result captured in Context for downstream actions. on_failure / on_success hooks fire as appropriate. Engine is pure — adapters injected.
acceptance_criteria: Tests with mock adapters: single-action workflow runs end-to-end; parallel actions execute concurrently; depends_on respected; failure mid-graph triggers on_failure; success triggers on_success; final RunState set correctly.

title: Core: action type contracts and scaffolds (no I/O yet)
description: src/youtrack_aitrack/domain/actions/. Define Action Protocol (async execute(ctx)->ActionResult). Skeletons (no real I/O): AiReportAction (just prompt rendering + stub LLM call), YtCommentAction (logs to console), SetFieldAction (logs to console). Real adapter integration lands in epic-003. Each registered via decorator. Pure dependency injection — adapters passed in constructor, defaults to no-op stubs.
acceptance_criteria: Each action type instantiates with injected dependencies. execute() returns ActionResult with success/failure. Tests assert dependency injection works and stubs do not call real services.

title: Core: YAML loader and workflow validation
description: src/youtrack_aitrack/config/loader.py. Load workflow YAML from path. Validate via pydantic Workflow model. Resolve env var references in YAML strings (e.g. ${YOUTRACK_URL}). Aggregate validation errors with file path and line numbers where possible. Schema export: dump JSON Schema from pydantic model for future UI editor.
acceptance_criteria: Valid YAML loads to Workflow object. Invalid YAML raises with helpful message. Env vars expanded at load time. JSON Schema export round-trips. Tests cover happy + several failure modes.

title: Core: plugin registry (decorator-based) for triggers and actions
description: src/youtrack_aitrack/registry/. Two registries: trigger_registry, action_registry. Decorator @register_trigger('name') and @register_action('name') attaches class to registry by string key. Lookup raises clear error on unknown type. Explicit init module loads all known plugins (no auto-scan). Type-safe via Protocol.
acceptance_criteria: Registry rejects duplicate registrations. Lookup returns class. Unknown type raises with available-types listed in error. Tests cover registration, lookup, duplicate, unknown.

title: Core: trigger types — status_change and manual
description: src/youtrack_aitrack/domain/triggers/. Implement StatusChangeTrigger (matches IssueEvent on from_state/to_state with '*' wildcard). ManualTrigger (always matches when invoked via CLI run command). Both implement Protocol Trigger.matches(event)->bool. Register via decorator at module import.
acceptance_criteria: Unit tests: status_change matches correct from/to combos including wildcards; manual always matches; non-matching events return False; both registered under expected names.

title: Core: pydantic models for Workflow, Trigger, Action, Context, Run
description: Define the domain language as pure pydantic v2 models in src/youtrack_aitrack/domain/. Workflow (name, trigger, actions[], on_failure, on_success, context). Trigger (base + discriminated union). Action (base + discriminated union with id, type, depends_on, output spec). Context (immutable: issue, branch, diff, accumulated outputs). RunState enum (pending/running/done/failed). IssueEvent (incoming YT event). ActionResult. No I/O, no logic — types only. Discriminated unions via pydantic Field(discriminator='type').
acceptance_criteria: All models import cleanly. Tests assert validation errors on bad payloads. Example workflow YAML round-trips through model + dump. mypy --strict passes.

title: Bootstrap: src-layout directory structure and gitignore
description: Create skeleton: src/youtrack_aitrack/{domain,engine,registry,adapters/{youtrack,git,llm,storage},config,cli}/__init__.py + tests/{unit,integration,fixtures}/__init__.py + workflows/ + prompts/. .gitignore comprehensive Python: .venv, __pycache__, *.egg-info, dist, build, .ruff_cache, .mypy_cache, .pytest_cache, .coverage, htmlcov, .env, .idea (PyCharm), .vscode (VS Code per-user), .youtrack-aitrack-state/. Keep existing .beads/, .dolt/, *.db, .beads-credential-key, .claude/. Remove PyCharm scaffold main.py. .env.example with placeholders + comments: YOUTRACK_URL, YOUTRACK_TOKEN, ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, REPO_PATH, YOUTRACK_PROJECT.
acceptance_criteria: All directories present with __init__.py. .gitignore committed. .env.example committed with documenting comments per variable.

title: Bootstrap: ruff and mypy strict configuration
description: Configure ruff in pyproject.toml: line-length 100, select rule sets E/F/W/I/N/UP/B/A/C4/RUF, format-on-save compatible. Configure mypy --strict on src/ (no implicit Any, no untyped defs, disallow incomplete defs). Verify on empty scaffold.
acceptance_criteria: uv run ruff check, uv run ruff format --check, uv run mypy src all pass on empty scaffold.

title: Bootstrap: pyproject.toml with deps and uv setup
description: Foundation for all subsequent work. Create pyproject.toml: project metadata (name=youtrack-aitrack, Python 3.12+, MIT license), runtime deps (anthropic, httpx, typer, pydantic, pydantic-settings, pyyaml, jinja2, python-dotenv), dev deps (pytest, pytest-asyncio, pytest-mock, respx, ruff, mypy, pre-commit). CLI entry points youtrack-aitrack and yta alias. uv as build/dep manager.
acceptance_criteria: uv sync succeeds; uv.lock generated; uv run youtrack-aitrack --help and uv run yta --help return without error (even if stub commands).

title: Engine: graceful fallback when GitDiffAdapter.resolve_branch returns None
description:
A workflow should not hard-fail when a YouTrack issue has no matching branch in the local repo. That happens routinely for design tasks, infra tickets, etc.

Behaviour: when GitDiffAdapter.resolve_branch returns None, the engine MUST:
1. Skip actions whose inputs depend on git_diff (inspect ActionSpec.inputs).
2. Log a structured event (action skipped, reason: no branch).
3. Post an explanatory comment to the issue via CommentPoster (if a yt_comment hook is configured), or set a custom field, or both — wired declaratively in the workflow YAML.
4. Continue executing actions whose inputs do NOT depend on git_diff (e.g. metadata-only audits).

Touches engine/engine.py action scheduling. NEW: a way for an action spec to declare a 'requires' set that the scheduler can short-circuit on. This is a small engine extension, not a domain change.

Why this issue exists: silent total failure is the worst outcome for the user. Partial success + an explanation is far better. Filed from session handoff (changes.md, 2026-05-11).
acceptance_criteria: When git diff is unavailable, the engine skips diff-dependent actions and runs the rest. RunReport records skipped actions with a reason. Tests cover: workflow with mixed deps runs the non-diff actions and reports skips for the diff-dependent ones; workflow with only diff-dependent actions reports a clean 'no work' rather than failure.

title: Adapter/Domain: diff classifier and size limit
description:
Filter and bound git diffs before they reach the LLM.

Behaviour:
- Exclude lock files (package-lock.json, poetry.lock, uv.lock, Cargo.lock, Gemfile.lock, etc. — list configurable in InstanceConfig.defaults or a new section).
- Exclude vendor directories (node_modules, vendor/, .venv/) and generated assets (dist/, build/, *.min.js).
- Skip large binaries (size > N KB; N configurable, default 256 KB).
- If the resulting diff exceeds a token-ish size limit (default 200 KB), chunk it by file or pass through a summariser (cheap heuristic now: keep file names + first N lines per file, mark truncation).

Location: domain/inputs.py or adapters/git/classifier.py — TBD during design. Probably a pure function in domain (no I/O) callable by GitDiffAdapter after raw diff extraction.

Why this issue exists: large diffs eat tokens and dilute LLM output. Lock-file noise also distracts. Filed from session handoff (changes.md, 2026-05-11).
acceptance_criteria: A classifier function takes raw git-diff text + InstanceConfig (or defaults) and returns the filtered + size-bounded diff. Default exclusions cover lock files, common vendor dirs, generated assets, binaries above the size cap. Oversized diffs are chunked or truncated with an explicit '[truncated]' marker. Pure (no I/O). Tests cover each exclusion category, the size cap, and the truncation marker.

title: Engine: idempotency key for workflow runs
description:
Skip duplicate runs of the same workflow on the same logical event unless --force.

Key shape: issue_id + to_state + commit_sha (or a deterministic equivalent — confirm during design when poller cursor and git diff are wired). Stored alongside RunReport in JsonRunStore so the engine can answer 'has this combination been processed?' on each dispatch.

Touches: engine/engine.py (dispatch path), engine/run_store.py (lookup helper). Does NOT touch adapters.

CLI surface: 'youtrack-aitrack run <issue-id> --force' bypasses the dedup check (epic-004 wires the flag).

Why this issue exists: the activities feed plus polling will replay events on cursor recovery. Without dedup, a process restart re-runs every report and burns tokens. Filed from session handoff (changes.md, 2026-05-11).
acceptance_criteria: Engine dedups by an idempotency key (issue_id + state + commit_sha or equivalent) when dispatching. JsonRunStore exposes a lookup that returns True/False without loading the full RunReport. --force flag on the run command bypasses dedup (CLI wiring lives in epic-004, but the engine plumbing must be in place here). Tests cover: same key skipped on second dispatch; different key proceeds; --force bypasses.

title: Domain: Extend IssueEvent for activities-feed semantics
description:
Prerequisite for eay (YouTrackClient). Reason: YouTrack's activities feed delivers field_change records with previous + current values + actor. Packing those into IssueEvent.raw is untyped and forces matchers to sniff dicts; typed fields are cheaper than a refactor after we add a second event producer (webhook).

Changes in src/youtrack_aitrack/domain/event.py:
- Extend event_kind Literal to include 'field_change': Literal['status_change', 'field_change', 'manual'].
- Add optional fields (all default None for backward-compat with existing constructors):
    field_name: str | None = None
    from_value: str | None = None
    to_value: str | None = None
    actor: str | None = None

Update src/youtrack_aitrack/domain/triggers/status_change.py:
- matches() must accept BOTH event_kind values:
    - event_kind == 'status_change' with from_state/to_state (legacy path, existing tests).
    - event_kind == 'field_change' with field_name == 'State' (or the YT-canonical name — keep configurable via a module constant if uncertain) using from_value/to_value.
- Pure function. No I/O. (Audit of f8j already confirmed current matcher is pure.)

Pick ONE of the two paths during implementation and document the choice in the commit:
(a) coexist: matcher accepts either event_kind shape (most backward-compatible),
(b) migrate: status_change kind retained only for manual constructions in tests; field_change is canonical for poller output.

Tests:
- existing test_event.py + test_triggers.py + test_loader.py still pass.
- new tests: field_change event with field_name='State' + from_value/to_value matches StatusChangeTrigger; non-State field_change does NOT match; matcher remains pure (no I/O).

Hard rules (CLAUDE.md):
- Single commit; domain-only change. No adapter edits in the same commit.
- mypy --strict clean; ruff clean; pre-commit green.
acceptance_criteria: event_kind Literal includes 'field_change'. IssueEvent gains field_name/from_value/to_value/actor as optional fields with default None. StatusChangeTrigger.matches() handles both legacy 'status_change' and new 'field_change' shapes and remains pure. All existing tests pass; new tests cover field_change matching and non-State rejection.
close_reason: IssueEvent extended: event_kind now Literal['status_change','field_change','manual']; new optional fields field_name/from_value/to_value/actor (default None) for activities-feed semantics. Added module constant STATE_FIELD_NAME='State' (canonical YT field). StatusChangeTrigger.matches() chose COEXIST path (option a): accepts both legacy status_change shape (from_state/to_state) and new field_change shape (field_name=='State' + from_value/to_value). Pure function, no I/O — matcher purity audit (f8j) still holds. 7 new tests added (field_change happy path, wildcard from, non-State rejection, from/to mismatch; new IssueEvent field_change construction; new fields default None). All existing tests pass. eay now unblocked.

title: Domain/Engine: RunStore Protocol
description:
Prerequisite for adapter bbq (JsonRunStore). Per CLAUDE.md anti-drift rule 2, Protocols in core must land in a separate commit from the adapter that implements them.

Location: src/youtrack_aitrack/engine/run_store.py (new module) — RunStore is an engine concern (run lifecycle), not a domain concept. If a domain placement is preferred during design, flag and discuss.

Shape:
    class RunStore(Protocol):
        def save_run(self, report: RunReport) -> None: ...
        def load_run(self, run_id: str) -> RunReport | None: ...
        def save_cursor(self, token: str | None) -> None: ...
        def load_cursor(self) -> str | None: ...

Verify exact import name for RunReport in domain/run.py before filing the Protocol.

Tests: tests/unit/test_run_store.py — assert Protocol shape via a tiny in-memory mock; verify mypy accepts a class with matching methods as a RunStore.
acceptance_criteria: RunStore Protocol defined in engine. Methods: save_run, load_run, save_cursor, load_cursor. Type-checked by mypy strict. Test confirms a minimal implementation satisfies the Protocol.
close_reason: RunStore Protocol filed in engine/run_store.py with _InMemoryRunStore default. Added run_id field to RunReport (uuid4 hex default) — was missing and needed to honor the Protocol's load_run(run_id) signature; flagged in commit. 7 tests cover Protocol shape, run_id defaults+uniqueness+override, and InMemory round-trips. Unblocks adapter bbq.

title: Domain: GitDiffProvider Protocol
description:
Prerequisite for adapter jpv (GitDiffAdapter). Per CLAUDE.md anti-drift rule 2, Protocols in core must land in a separate commit from the adapter that implements them.

src/youtrack_aitrack/domain/inputs.py (NEW MODULE — flag for design discussion if a different location makes more sense): define GitDiffProvider Protocol.

Shape:
    class GitDiffProvider(Protocol):
        def resolve_branch(self, task_id: str, *, repo_dir: Path, pattern: str) -> str | None: ...
        def diff(self, repo_dir: Path, branch: str, base: str = 'main') -> str: ...

No implementation. Pure Protocol. Add a NoOp implementation in the same file if useful for engine wiring (mirror the pattern in domain/actions/ai_report.py: _NoOpLLM, _IdentityRenderer).

Tests: tests/unit/test_inputs.py — assert Protocol shape via a small mock that satisfies it, and that the NoOp (if added) returns sensible defaults.
acceptance_criteria: GitDiffProvider Protocol defined. Methods: resolve_branch and diff. Type-checked by mypy strict. Test asserts a minimal implementation satisfies the Protocol.
close_reason: GitDiffProvider Protocol filed in domain/inputs.py with _NoOpGitDiffProvider default, 4 tests verify Protocol shape and NoOp behaviour. Unblocks adapter jpv.

title: Adapter: JsonRunStore (RunReport + poll-cursor persistence)
description:
src/youtrack_aitrack/adapters/storage/runs.py. JSON-on-disk store for two concerns:

(1) Persist RunReport-shaped objects (domain/run.py — verify exact name) per run, keyed by run-id, under <config-dir>/runs/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<run-id>.json. Atomic write via tmp+rename. Read-back by run-id.

(2) Persist the last-seen polling cursor (from YouTrackClient.changed_issues_since) under <config-dir>/runs/.cursor.json — single-key JSON, atomic write.

Required Protocol does NOT exist yet. PREREQUISITE separate commit (per CLAUDE.md anti-drift rule 2): define RunStore Protocol in engine (or domain/run.py). Shape: 'def save_run(report: RunReport) -> None', 'def load_run(run_id: str) -> RunReport | None', 'def save_cursor(token: str | None) -> None', 'def load_cursor() -> str | None'. File this Protocol issue separately; this adapter issue blocks on it.

Constructor: JsonRunStore(runs_dir: Path).

Tests: tests/unit/test_adapter_runs.py with tmp_path. Cover: save+load round-trip, cursor round-trip, atomic write semantics (writes to tmp file first), corrupt JSON returns None / raises a typed error (decide and document), unknown run_id returns None.
acceptance_criteria: JsonRunStore implements the RunStore Protocol (filed separately first). Save/load round-trips for RunReport and cursor. Atomic writes via tmp+rename. Corrupt JSON handled deterministically. Tests use tmp_path.
close_reason: JsonRunStore implements RunStore Protocol. save_run writes <runs_dir>/<YYYY-MM-DD>/<run_id>.json via tmp+rename (atomic). load_run scans date subdirs newest-first, returns RunReport or None. save_cursor/load_cursor read+write <runs_dir>/.cursor.json with {'cursor': str|null} shape. Corrupt JSON or unexpected shape raises typed JsonRunStoreError (fail-loud on bad data; None reserved for 'not present'). 16 tests cover Protocol shape, round-trip, dated subdir, overwrite same id, multi-day scan, missing dir, dotfile ignore, corrupt+shape errors, atomic write.

title: Adapter: GitDiffAdapter (branch resolution + diff extraction)
description:
src/youtrack_aitrack/adapters/git/diff.py. Subprocess wrapper around git for the workflow input 'git_diff' (referenced by AiReportAction.inputs).

Required Protocol does NOT exist yet. PREREQUISITE separate commit (per CLAUDE.md anti-drift rule 2): add a GitDiffProvider Protocol to domain (likely domain/inputs.py — a new module — or attached to a context input registry). Shape: 'def resolve_branch(task_id: str, *, repo_dir: Path, pattern: str) -> str | None' and 'def diff(repo_dir: Path, branch: str, base: str = "main") -> str'. File this Protocol issue separately; this adapter issue blocks on it.

Adapter behaviour:
- resolve_branch: list local + remote branches, filter by branch_pattern (uses {task_id} placeholder from InstanceConfig.defaults.branch_pattern), return the single match or None.
- diff: run 'git diff --merge-base <base> <branch>' (subprocess.run with check=True, capture_output, timeout). Return stdout decoded utf-8.

Constructor: GitDiffAdapter(*, git_executable: str = 'git'). No env reads.

Tests: tests/unit/test_adapter_git.py with tmp_path initialising a real tiny git repo (subprocess git init + commits) — fast and deterministic. Cover: branch resolution finds match, ambiguous match returns None or raises (decide during implementation, document the choice), diff returns expected text, subprocess failures map to a typed error.
acceptance_criteria: GitDiffAdapter implements the GitDiffProvider Protocol (filed separately first). resolve_branch matches by configured pattern. diff() runs 'git diff --merge-base base branch' and returns stdout. Subprocess failures raise a typed adapter error. Tests use tmp_path with a real local git repo, never the project's own repo.
close_reason: GitDiffAdapter implements GitDiffProvider Protocol. subprocess wraps the git CLI with check=True, capture_output, text mode, 30s timeout. resolve_branch lists local+remote refs via 'git branch --list --all <pattern>', strips HEAD pointers and remotes/<remote>/ prefix, dedups, returns single match or None — ambiguous match raises typed GitDiffError (chose loud failure over silent skip; engine fallback 1ud handles the None case explicitly). diff runs 'git diff --merge-base <base> <branch>'. Subprocess failures (CalledProcessError, TimeoutExpired, FileNotFoundError) all map to GitDiffError. 10 tests cover Protocol shape, single match, no match, ambiguous, pattern without {task_id}, diff content, empty diff, bad branch, missing git binary, local+remote dedup. Real local git repos in tmp_path; never touches the project repo.

title: Adapter: YouTrackClient (FieldWriter + CommentPoster + polling)
description:
src/youtrack_aitrack/adapters/youtrack/client.py. Implement THREE concerns in one client class:

1) FieldWriter Protocol (domain/actions/set_field.py):
   async def set_fields(self, issue_id: str, fields: dict[str, str]) -> None

2) CommentPoster Protocol (domain/actions/yt_comment.py):
   async def post_comment(self, issue_id: str, body: str) -> None

3) Polling primitive (engine-facing; Protocol formalised in epic-004):
   async def changed_issues_since(self, cursor: str | None) -> tuple[list[IssueEvent], str]

POLLING SHAPE — locked per session handoff (changes.md):

- Hit YouTrack's ACTIVITIES feed, NOT /api/issues snapshots. Endpoint: /api/activities or /api/issues/{id}/activities. The activities feed gives field-change records with previous + current values + actor; an issue snapshot does not. This is what lets StatusChangeTrigger match without extra lookups.
- Map each activity into an IssueEvent. After issue wf6 lands, populate event_kind='field_change', field_name, from_value, to_value, actor, timestamp, issue_id, project, raw (the original activity payload as escape hatch).
- For state-transition activities (field_name == YouTrack's State field name): the emitted IssueEvent MUST carry from_value and to_value populated, so StatusChangeTrigger matches without sniffing raw.
- Cursor is YouTrack's activities-feed resumption token (timestamp+id, or opaque string — confirm during implementation). Round-trip through JsonRunStore.save_cursor / load_cursor unchanged.

STACK: httpx.AsyncClient with bearer-token auth header. Constructor: YouTrackClient(base_url, token, *, project, http: httpx.AsyncClient | None = None). Inject http for tests.

CUSTOM-FIELD WRITES: YouTrack REST treats custom fields as a list of objects on POST /api/issues/{id}. Resolve field name -> field id at first use, cache the mapping per YouTrackClient instance. Simple-typed fields only for now (string/text); enum/state can be deferred to a follow-up.

FIELD-ID CACHE INVARIANT: cache survives across calls within a single YouTrackClient instance. NOT persisted to disk. A YT admin renaming a custom field should fail loud and refetch on the next process start.

ERROR MAPPING: 4xx and 5xx map to a typed YouTrackError (adapters/youtrack/errors.py if a dedicated module is helpful, otherwise inline).

TESTS: tests/unit/test_adapter_youtrack.py with respx mounted on a stub base_url. Cover:
- set_fields hits POST /api/issues/{id} with the correct field-id payload after one-time GET of the field metadata.
- post_comment hits the comments endpoint with the right body.
- changed_issues_since: round-trip cursor; emitted events for state transitions carry from_value/to_value populated; non-State field_change activities are emitted but won't trigger StatusChangeTrigger (covered in trigger tests, not here).
- 4xx response raises typed YouTrackError.
- Field-id cache: two set_fields calls in a row issue only ONE GET to resolve the field id.

Maps to two domain Protocols (FieldWriter, CommentPoster) already filed; no new Protocol needed for those. The 'changed_issues_since' shape is internal until epic-004 defines the engine-facing Poller Protocol.
acceptance_criteria: YouTrackClient implements FieldWriter and CommentPoster. set_fields and post_comment hit the correct REST endpoints with correct payloads. Field-name -> field-id resolution is cached per instance (survives across calls within a single YouTrackClient instance; not persisted to disk). changed_issues_since reads YouTrack's ACTIVITIES feed and emits IssueEvent objects with event_kind='field_change' populated; for state transitions field_name/from_value/to_value/actor are populated. Cursor round-trips through JsonRunStore unchanged. 4xx responses raise a typed YouTrackError. Tests use respx — no real network — and include an assertion that two set_fields calls only fetch field metadata ONCE.
close_reason: YouTrackClient shipped: FieldWriter+CommentPoster+activities-feed polling. Return type widened to tuple[list[IssueEvent], str | None] (vs locked tuple[..., str]) so cursor round-trips cleanly with JsonRunStore's str|None shape. 11 respx tests cover payload shape (Simple+Text), field-id cache (1 GET across 2 set_fields), comments endpoint, state vs non-state event mapping, project filter, 4xx -> YouTrackError, unknown field -> YouTrackError.

title: Adapter: JinjaPromptRenderer
description:
src/youtrack_aitrack/adapters/llm/jinja.py. Implement the existing PromptRenderer Protocol (domain/actions/ai_report.py): 'def render(self, template: str, ctx: Context) -> str'.

Interpretation: 'template' is a path-like string resolved against InstanceConfig.prompts_path(config_dir). Load the file once, cache the jinja Template by filesystem path. Render with a dict view of Context exposed under 'ctx' (use ctx.model_dump() — Context is a pydantic model).

Constructor: JinjaPromptRenderer(prompts_dir: Path). Use jinja2.Environment with FileSystemLoader(prompts_dir), autoescape=False (prompts are plain text, not HTML), keep_trailing_newline=True. StrictUndefined so missing context fields fail loudly.

Tests: tests/unit/test_adapter_jinja.py with tmp_path. Cover: simple substitution, accessing nested ctx.issue.issue_id, missing template raises, missing variable raises (StrictUndefined), repeated render uses cached template object.
acceptance_criteria: JinjaPromptRenderer implements PromptRenderer Protocol. Template path resolved against prompts_dir. ctx.model_dump() exposed as 'ctx' in the template. StrictUndefined raises on missing variable. Missing template file raises a clear error. Tests use tmp_path.
close_reason: JinjaPromptRenderer implements PromptRenderer Protocol via jinja2 Environment + FileSystemLoader rooted at prompts_dir. Uses StrictUndefined (missing var raises UndefinedError), autoescape=False (prompts are text), keep_trailing_newline=True, auto_reload=False (templates cached after first load). render() exposes ctx.model_dump() as 'ctx'. Missing template raises FileNotFoundError. 7 tests cover Protocol shape, substitution, nested access, strict undefined, file-not-found, cache reuse, subdirs.

title: Adapter: AnthropicLLMClient (anthropic SDK)
description:
src/youtrack_aitrack/adapters/llm/anthropic.py. Implement the existing LLMClient Protocol (domain/actions/ai_report.py): 'async def complete(self, prompt: str, model: str) -> str'. Wrap the anthropic SDK (already a project dep) — use AsyncAnthropic with API key from constructor argument (no global state). Map prompt -> messages with a single user-role message. Return the concatenated text content from response.content.

Constructor: AnthropicLLMClient(api_key: str, *, base_url: str | None = None, max_tokens: int = 4096, timeout_seconds: float = 60.0). Defensible defaults; no env reads inside the adapter — InstanceConfig already loads the api_key.

Tests: tests/unit/test_adapter_anthropic.py. Mock the SDK client at construction (inject a fake AsyncAnthropic-shaped object via a constructor seam) — DO NOT call the real API. Cover: happy path returns text, model arg is forwarded, multi-block content is concatenated, error from SDK propagates.
acceptance_criteria: AnthropicLLMClient implements LLMClient Protocol. Constructor takes api_key (no env reads). complete() forwards model arg. Multi-block response content is concatenated. SDK errors propagate. No real API calls in tests.
close_reason: AnthropicLLMClient wraps AsyncAnthropic, implements LLMClient Protocol. Constructor accepts api_key + base_url/max_tokens/timeout, with a client= seam for tests. complete() builds a single user message, returns concatenated text from TextBlock entries. 7 tests cover Protocol shape, model/prompt forwarding, multi-block concatenation, non-text block skipping, error propagation, custom max_tokens. No real API calls.

title: Epic: Adapters layer (I/O implementations)
description:
Build the five I/O adapters that let workflows actually reach external systems. Until these land, AiReportAction/SetFieldAction/YtCommentAction fall back to no-op stubs. After this epic closes, only the reference workflow (epic-003) and run/poll CLI wiring (epic-004) stand between today and a daemon that processes real YouTrack events.

Scope:
- adapters/llm/anthropic.py: implements LLMClient Protocol via anthropic SDK
- adapters/llm/jinja.py: implements PromptRenderer Protocol via jinja2
- adapters/youtrack/client.py: implements FieldWriter + CommentPoster + polling cursor
- adapters/git/diff.py: subprocess git for branch resolution + diff extraction (defines new Protocol)
- adapters/storage/runs.py: JSON-on-disk RunReport store + last-poll cursor (defines new Protocol)

Hard rules (CLAUDE.md):
- Each adapter = one issue = one commit. No bundling.
- For adapters that need a NEW Protocol (git diff, run store), the Protocol must land in a SEPARATE prior commit per anti-drift rule 2.
- Adapters wrap I/O only — no business logic. Engine talks via Protocols.
- Contract-tested with respx (HTTP) and tmp_path (filesystem).

title: CLI: workflows list and workflows validate subcommands
description:
src/youtrack_aitrack/cli/workflows.py. Typer sub-app exposing two subcommands:

'youtrack-aitrack workflows list' — read InstanceConfig, scan paths.workflows_dir for *.yaml, attempt load_workflow on each, print a table: name | trigger type | action count. On parse failure, print the file name and the first-line of the WorkflowParseError but continue. Always exits 0. Useful for discovery.

'youtrack-aitrack workflows validate' — same scan loop, but exits non-zero if ANY file fails to load. Quiet on success unless --verbose. Suitable for CI / pre-deploy hooks.

Both commands accept --config-dir <path> (precedence rules from issue 759) and resolve the workflows directory through InstanceConfig.workflows_path(config_dir).

Output formatting: use typer.echo with simple alignment, no Rich tables for now (keep dependencies tight; Rich isn't a project dep yet). Error lines prefixed with 'ERROR: <filename>: <message>'.

Tests: use tmp_path with two YAML files (one valid, one with a known parse error), assert list prints both with the error annotated and exits 0; assert validate exits 1 and names the broken file.
acceptance_criteria: With a config dir containing one valid workflow YAML and one invalid YAML, 'workflows list' prints both files (one with an error annotation) and exits 0. 'workflows validate' exits 1 and names the broken file. Both commands respect --config-dir, $YOUTRACK_AITRACK_HOME, and the default ~/.youtrack-aitrack/ in that precedence order. No real home directory accessed during tests.
close_reason: kay: workflows list/validate subcommands implemented (cli/workflows.py, 8 tests). dr1: epic-002 closes — 3v8 + 759 + kay all merged. CLI workflow administration shipped: init scaffolds config, workflows list/validate inspect YAML.

title: CLI: init command scaffolds the config directory
description:
src/youtrack_aitrack/cli/init.py. Typer subcommand 'youtrack-aitrack init' that creates the config directory (default ~/.youtrack-aitrack/, overridable via $YOUTRACK_AITRACK_HOME) and populates it with: config.yaml (template referencing ${YOUTRACK_URL}, ${YOUTRACK_TOKEN}, ${YOUTRACK_PROJECT}, ${ANTHROPIC_API_KEY}), .env.example (committed-friendly placeholder file listing required env-var names), workflows/ (empty, with .gitkeep), prompts/ (empty, with .gitkeep), runs/ (empty, with .gitkeep).

Idempotent: each file/directory check-and-skip individually. --force flag overwrites existing files. --config-dir <path> overrides the default location explicitly (precedence: --config-dir > $YOUTRACK_AITRACK_HOME > ~/.youtrack-aitrack).

cli/main.py gains a load_dotenv() call at startup (BEFORE any subcommand runs) that loads <config-dir>/.env if present. Use python-dotenv (already a project dep). Document this behaviour in the init template config.yaml comments.

config.yaml template uses the field structure from InstanceConfig (this issue depends on 3v8). default_model in template is 'claude-sonnet-4-6'; branch_pattern is '{task_id}-*'.

Acceptance criteria covered separately.
acceptance_criteria: Running 'youtrack-aitrack init' against a tmp_path produces a directory layout that load_instance_config can read once env vars are set. Re-running 'init' is a no-op (no files overwritten). 'init --force' rewrites the template files. $YOUTRACK_AITRACK_HOME overrides the default location. --config-dir overrides both. Tests use tmp_path and monkeypatched env, never the real home directory.
close_reason: Implemented init subcommand + config_dir resolver. Scaffolds config.yaml, .env.example, workflows/prompts/runs subdirs with .gitkeep. Idempotent with --force override. Root callback wires --config-dir flag and auto-loads <config-dir>/.env via python-dotenv. 13 tests cover precedence, idempotency, force, dotenv autoload, and round-trip with load_instance_config.

title: CLI: InstanceConfig pydantic model and loader
description:
src/youtrack_aitrack/config/instance.py. Pydantic model InstanceConfig with sections: youtrack (url, token, project), anthropic (api_key, default_model), paths (workflows_dir, prompts_dir, runs_dir — all relative to config dir), defaults (branch_pattern, poll_interval_seconds). Loader function load_instance_config(path, env=None) mirrors load_workflow: reads YAML, expands ${VAR} via the existing config.loader.expand_env, validates via pydantic, raises a typed error (InstanceConfigError) with file/line on failure. Default model literal: 'claude-sonnet-4-6'. Default branch_pattern: '{task_id}-*'. paths fields default to relative names ('workflows', 'prompts', 'runs') so a freshly-init'd config dir works without overrides.

Resolution helper on the model: instance.workflows_path(config_dir: Path) -> Path returns config_dir / paths.workflows_dir; same for prompts and runs. Keeps relative-path logic in one place.

Acceptance: valid YAML loads; missing required field raises InstanceConfigError with the missing path; env-var expansion works; tests cover happy path + 4 failure modes.
acceptance_criteria: Valid YAML loads to InstanceConfig. Required-field omission raises InstanceConfigError naming the missing field. Env-var ${VAR} expansion works in token/api_key fields. workflows_path()/prompts_path()/runs_path() helpers return the resolved Path. Tests: happy + missing required + env expansion + custom paths + invalid YAML.
close_reason: Implemented InstanceConfig model + load_instance_config in src/youtrack_aitrack/config/instance.py with full test coverage (8 tests, all acceptance criteria met).

title: Enable branch protection / ruleset on main once repo is public
description: Branch protection (classic API and rulesets API) is blocked on free private repos with HTTP 403 'Upgrade to GitHub Pro or make this repository public.' The j1j acceptance criterion 'Failing gate blocks merge' is therefore satisfied only visually (PR UI shows red checks) until the repo is flipped to public or upgraded to Pro. When the repo goes public, run the gh api PUT to /repos/PanzerLlama/youtrack-aitrack/branches/main/protection (or POST a ruleset) requiring the 'Lint, types, tests' status context, with strict=true so branches must be up-to-date before merging. Verify with gh api /repos/PanzerLlama/youtrack-aitrack/branches/main/protection.

title: Domain: validate depends_on in on_success and on_failure groups
description: Workflow._check_depends_on_resolves currently only checks self.actions[*].depends_on. Specs in on_success and on_failure can declare depends_on values that are silently ignored at validation time and will not be honored by the engine. Either extend the validator across all groups (with action_ids drawn from main actions plus same-group ids) or reject depends_on outside the main actions list. Add tests covering both groups.
acceptance_criteria: Workflow construction with bogus depends_on in on_success or on_failure raises ValidationError. Tests cover the new rejections.

title: Tooling: scripts/verify-hooks.sh integrity check
description: The pre-commit framework chain lives in .beads/hooks/pre-commit below bd's BEGIN/END markers. If bd ever rewrites the file (major version bump, recovery), the integration could vanish silently. Add scripts/verify-hooks.sh that asserts 'uv run pre-commit run' is present in the hook. Wire into CI (j1j) and/or scripts/setup-dev.sh.
acceptance_criteria: verify-hooks.sh exits 0 when chain intact, non-zero with a clear error message when missing. Called from CI and from setup-dev.sh.

title: Tooling: scripts/setup-dev.sh and CONTRIBUTING quickstart
description: Fresh-clone onboarding currently requires trial-and-error: installing uv on PEP-668 systems via 'pip install --user --break-system-packages' is ugly and Ubuntu-specific. Add scripts/setup-dev.sh that installs uv via the official Astral installer (or pipx fallback), runs uv sync, verifies pre-commit hooks are wired (calls verify-hooks.sh), and runs gates as a smoke test. Document the entry point in CONTRIBUTING.md.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh checkout + ./scripts/setup-dev.sh produces a working dev environment with all gates passing on a stock Ubuntu 24+ machine without manual intervention.

title: Tooling: pin Python to 3.12 via .python-version
description: uv selects the latest available Python (3.13.5) while pyproject only requires >=3.12. CI and teammate machines may resolve to different minor versions, producing subtle typing, lint and stdlib behaviour drift. Pin to 3.12 (lowest supported) via .python-version so uv reproducibly resolves the same minor everywhere.
acceptance_criteria: .python-version present at repo root with content 3.12. uv sync recreates the venv with Python 3.12.x. All gates green on 3.12.

title: Tooling: portable pre-commit + bd hooks setup script
description: Current pre-commit framework integration is patched into .beads/hooks/pre-commit which is gitignored. Fresh clones get bd hooks via 'bd init' but lose our pre-commit chaining. Add scripts/install-hooks.sh that re-applies the integration, document in CONTRIBUTING.md (and check on dev setup). Optionally explore moving hooks to a tracked, project-owned dir referenced via core.hooksPath.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh checkout + ./scripts/install-hooks.sh produces a working pre-commit + bd hook chain. README/CONTRIBUTING reference the script.
close_reason: False alarm: .beads/hooks/* is already tracked in git, so the bd-hook chained pre-commit integration is portable across clones via the regular commit flow.

title: Tooling: track .beads/issues.jsonl in git
description: bd auto-exports issues to .beads/issues.jsonl on every state change but the file sits inside gitignored .beads/, producing repeated 'auto-export: git add failed' warnings. JSONL is the canonical shared-issue format intended to be versioned. Update .gitignore to ignore .beads/* except issues.jsonl, then track the existing export.
acceptance_criteria: bd close or update no longer prints 'auto-export: git add failed'. .beads/issues.jsonl is tracked in git; .beads/beads.db and other local state remain ignored.

value: epic-002 (CLI workflow administration) design decisions, locked 2026-05-09. (1) Config dir defaults to ~/.youtrack-aitrack/, overridable via env var $YOUTRACK_AITRACK_HOME, and via CLI flag --config-dir (precedence: --config-dir > $YOUTRACK_AITRACK_HOME > default). (2) Prompt paths in workflow YAML resolve relative to InstanceConfig.paths.prompts_dir, NOT relative to the workflow file.
